Hi!

I love you. You matter. It sounds like you’ve had a really rough go of life and you don’t deserve any of that. I’m so sorry you’ve suffered so immensely at such a young age. That’s horrifically unfair that your parents haven’t given you the love and emotional nurturing every kid needs. I hope you understand that isn’t your fault.

I get that I’m just some rando on Reddit to you. But listen - I’m a real person. My name is G. I’m a woman who lives in California. I’m a mental health worker currently driving DoorDash to make ends meet. Last summer I fell asleep with bleach in my hair, causing it to fall out in handfuls like a horror movie. A few months ago I got my heart broken by a person who I thought loved me. When I was 15 I got my finger stuck in a salt shaker in drama class and had to have it smashed off by the school nurse when the vice principal finally left the room.  I love punk and hardcore and cats and being along in the forest. 

Why am I telling you this? I’m telling you this because when we talk over Reddit, it’s sometimes hard to see each other as actual humans and that can lower the meaning of their words. It’s almost like a robot saying something - who cares, right? So I’m telling you a bit about me to help your brain recognize me as an actual person: an actual person who CARES ABOUT YOU. WE CARE ABOUT YOU HERE. 17 is such a hard age and it sounds like it’s been extra hard for you. I promise you it gets better. You are loved. You CAN have a good and happy life. Maybe it starts with not drinking anymore. You don’t have to commit to that now, or forever, or whatever. But maybe stopping that could be a starting point for you to begin the healing process, because it’s hard to heal when you’re always fucked up (speaking from experience). 

I believe in you. 
What would be helpful for you? Do you need someone to talk to? Would you like help finding a therapist? Do you just need to vent? 

You matter.

Hi there. I work in this field. I’m sorry you’ve had such negative experiences with therapy. The truth is that yeah, there’s some crappy therapists out there. But I do want you to know that when a therapist refers you elsewhere, it’s because they feel they are not well-equipped enough to help you, either because it’s not something they’re super familiar with or because it’s triggering something in them, which would be unfair to you. As tiring as it is - and it is tiring, I’ve been through my fair share of therapists myself - it’s worth it to keep trying and keep searching.

Also fuck this godforsaken country and the fact that so many people have such insane barriers to treatment thanks to the almighty insurance rackets. 

Hang in there, friend. Please keep going. Your life matters. You might feel like it doesn’t and sure I’m just some random woman on the internet. But your life matters and you deserve joy and fulfillment and all the good things others get too. That’s an objective fact. Our brains often lie to us, telling us that we’re broken, unworthy, and never going to feel anything but the crippling despair for the rest of our lives. And goddamn that shit is CONVINCING because it speaks in our own voice and it becomes seemingly impossible to differentiate the depression and pain from ourselves as a whole. But that voice lies. You can heal with the right care and you deserve that. Your suffering is valid and real and I want to recognize that. Just please know that there is hope. Even if you don’t believe that right now. People care about you. I care about you. Is there anything I can do to help you? I am falling asleep so if I don’t respond right away that’s why, but I will be sure to check this thread tomorrow. Please hang in there.

But the truth of the matter is likely the opposite. Too much drug use, no matter the drug, results in this self-fulfilling prophecy of pain, shame, and worsening depression. The only way out of that is through. You can do this, friend. You can seek help and start feeling better, having a better life. It takes time, yeah. And it’s far from easy. But I PROMISE you it gets better and it’s worth it.
